brief: Claude dominated today's posts, with Claude Ship in beta, Claude plugins combining connectors and skills, and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in public beta. Beyond that, Replit published research on scaling laws for agent swarms, finding that organization matters as much as agent count.

themes.label: Claude Ship and code review
themes.summary: Boris Cherny said Claude Ship is in beta for Team and Enterprise, pairing Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals to handle PRs.

themes.label: Claude plugins and safeguards
themes.summary: Anthropic's Claude account announced plugins that merge connectors and skills, plus Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in public beta with zero data retention.

themes.label: Agent swarm scaling research
themes.summary: Amjad Masad shared Replit research finding that agent swarm results depend on how agents organize, with decentralized swarms scaling better.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Shared Replit research on agent swarm scaling laws, showing decentralized swarms scaled better than centralized ones. He also discussed American open-weight AI leadership in a meeting with VP JD Vance.

builders.name: Boris Cherny
builders.summary: Launched Claude Ship in beta for Team and Enterprise plans and described Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals. He said the tools multiply his velocity.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary: Announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in public beta with zero data retention, and launched plugins combining connectors and skills across plans.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Said a personal eval of his coding sessions picked Gemini Neon over Opus. He also posted about Vercel expanding in Japan.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Argued that agents decouple services output from headcount, so one engineer or designer can produce what many once did.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Excited about a proactive agent launch that needs no prompting. He also wrote about America's appeal to ambitious builders abroad.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Shared a startup tip to ask 'are we dying?' in a loop to spot threats early.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Praised X payouts as a model for lean software companies that reward users who help them grow.

builders.name: Madhu Guru
builders.summary: Argued that data encodes high value knowledge, taste and expertise and is central to model development. He also announced a planned meetup.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Urged builders to create personal benchmarks and shared a guide to making one.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Argued that people can post daily and still be private by sharing only what is interesting and comfortable. She also shared a guide to preventing AI slop in design.

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Posted light commentary on AI news in November and a joke about 2027 job titles built around swarms.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Highlighted OpenAI work patching open-source software and said ChatGPT answer quality will improve by year end. He also noted dots are becoming a primary way to get work done at OpenAI.

builders.name: Sam Altman
builders.summary: Shared a link he called really good and posted a short reply about Jensen.

builders.name: Matt Turck
builders.summary: Posted brief commentary on Jensen returning and a joke about AI news.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Reported that ChatGPT Dots still feels buggy, sending emails without review and stopping responses. Other posts are personal or minor.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Reacted to a Microsoft effort and suggested Alexandr Wang join to unite labs. Other posts are minor.
